TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Evidence shows vorinostat engaged its target - HP1 and MacroH2A nuclear foci expression changes were observed, with measurable biomarker changes including MacroH2A1.1 (0.149 log fold change), MacroH2A1.2 (-0.748 log fold change), and HP1 (-0.077 log fold change). This confirms HDAC inhibition occurred. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The biomarker changes in chromatin-associated proteins (HP1, MacroH2A) indicate downstream chromatin remodeling occurred as expected from HDAC inhibition. VEGF levels also changed significantly (p=0.029), suggesting pathway engagement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite target engagement and pathway modulation, the primary endpoint failed - only 2/32 patients (6.25%) achieved objective response, well below any meaningful threshold for melanoma. Time to progression also failed. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Subgroup analysis showed p53 wild type (20 patients) vs mutant (11 patients) but no differential response data reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm Phase 2 trial with adequate sample size (n=32) and long duration (260 weeks). Safety profile showed multiple serious adverse events but no dose-limiting toxicity that would prevent adequate target engagement.
